question: A 49-year-old female with a long history of poorly controlled diabetes mellitus visits her primary care physician with 2+ non-pitting edema in her legs. The patient has a serum creatinine of 2.9 mg/dL and a blood urea nitrogen of 61 mg/dL. A 24-hour urine collection reveals 8.5 grams of protein. A renal biopsy is obtained. Which of the following histologic findings is most likely to be seen upon tissue analysis:?

options.opb: Nodular thickening of the glomerular basement membrane

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus -> diabetic nephropathy -> renal dysfunction -> 80% CHAIN: Renal dysfunction -> proteinuria -> 8.5 grams of protein in 24-hour urine collection -> 70% CHAIN: Proteinuria -> glomerular injury -> renal biopsy -> 60% CHAIN: Glomerular injury -> nodular thickening of the glomerular basement membrane -> 80%
enhanced_information: In a patient with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus presenting with significant proteinuria, the most likely histologic finding upon renal biopsy would be nodular thickening of the glomerular basement membrane, consistent with diabetic nephropathy.
analysis: In a patient with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus and significant proteinuria, the most likely histologic finding upon renal biopsy is nodular thickening of the glomerular basement membrane, consistent with diabetic nephropathy. This is a well-established association in diabetic patients.
